description: Eleven Win32-backend failures are tests that cannot run on the Win32 runner as written: test_semantic_input.py:215 `_spec` builds `LibSpec(backend="x64", dll=str(portlib.path))` and under SG_BACKEND=win32 `portlib.path` is portsim_runner32.exe, so `CDLL` raises WinError 193 (4 tests here, 4 in test_integrator through the same loader); test_holestats' two `clock queries ... served` tests read `run_detail`, which is '' because Lib32 has no `.dll` (integrator.run_detail returns '' when `dll` is None); test_tick::test_run_frames_reports_why_it_stopped reads `lib.dll.sg_run_frames_detail` (NoneType). Read from the tracebacks in log/roadmap/S0/1_suite_win32/ and the code at HEAD 4bfefc2a.
path to resolution: Make the three helpers backend-aware (spec from the backend, run_detail over a runner op) or mark the tests x64-only; until then the 11 failures are the Win32 baseline.

description: Nine Win32-backend test failures are not diagnosed: test_golden_digests in test_browser (20 scenarios differ from the pinned digests), test_course_menu (3: save_dialog, load_then_cancel, load_a_game), test_save_dialogs (22) and test_saveload (12), and the five test_saveload `test_save_writes_the_loaded_body_back_byte_for_byte[...]` tests, whose `<tmp>/install/Saved Games/roundtrip.sve` is missing after saveGame ran with `st.files_root(root)` set (x64: present, 5 / 5 pass). The same files pass on x64 with the same pinned digests. A probe (log/roadmap/S0/1_probe_files_root.py) shows files_put followed by files_size / files_read agree on both backends and `files_root` returns None on both; the probe does not run the game's own save, so it does not separate a runner32 write-through defect from a digest that depends on the backend. Observed only: the failing keys are the browser / load / save scenarios.
path to resolution: Run one failing key on both backends with SG_TICK_DUMP / the call log and diff the file operations; check runner32.cpp op 23 (files_root) against the Win32 DLL's write path.
